en.title: Minister Zameer sends Independence Day greetings to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Georgia
en.description: His Excellency Mr. Moosa Zameer, Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, sends a message of greetings to His Excellency Mr. Ilia Darchiashvili, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Georgia, on the occasion of Georgia’s Independence Day.
en.body:
His Excellency Mr. Moosa Zameer, Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, sends a message of greetings to His Excellency Mr. Ilia Darchiashvili, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Georgia, on the occasion of Georgia’s Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, it gives me great pleasure to extend sincere greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Georgia, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Georgia.

The ties between Maldives and Georgia have stood the test of time, fostering a strong bond between the two nations. It is my hope that our friendly relations continue to provide a fruitful, mutually beneficial partnership that lasts into the future.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for you and your people on this auspicious day, and the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: The President arrives in Antigua and Barbuda for the 4th International Conference on SIDS
en.description: President Dr Mohamed Muizzu has arrived in Antigua and Barbuda to participate in the fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS).
en.body:
President Dr Mohamed Muizzu has arrived in Antigua and Barbuda to participate in the fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS).

During the Summit, President Dr Mohamed Muizzu will deliver the National Statement at the plenary of the Summit on May 27, 2024. Additionally, he is scheduled to meet with several foreign dignitaries and deliver remarks at some of the side events of the Summit.

President Dr Muizzu is also one of the Vice Presidents of the conference as well as co-chair of one of the five interactive dialogues organised by the United Nations (UN) at the conference.

The UN holds the Conference on SIDS once a decade. One of the highlights of the fourth International Conference on SIDS is the adoption of the new Programme of Action, the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS. This years conference is held under the overarching theme of "charting the course toward resilient prosperity."

Source: <https://presidency.gov.mv/Press/Article/30801>

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Independence Day greetings to Jordan

en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of felicitations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs and Expatriates of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, His Excellency Ayman Safadi on the occasion of Jordan’s Independence Day.

"It is my great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere felicitations to Your Excellency, the Government and the friendly people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, on the grand occasion of Jordan's Independence Day.

en.title: The Government of Maldives welcomes the order issued by the International Court of Justice calling on Israel to halt all military offensive in Rafah
en.description: The Government of Maldives welcomes the Order issued by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on the request for the modification and indication of further provisional measures submitted by South Africa in the case “Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of…
en.body:
The Government of Maldives welcomes the Order issued by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on the request for the modification and indication of further provisional measures submitted by South Africa in the case “Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel)”.

The ICJ in its order, today, called on Israel to immediately halt its military offensive in Rafah and open the Rafah crossing for unhindered delivery of urgently needed basic services and humanitarian assistance. The Court also ordered Israel to ensure unimpeded access to the Gaza Strip for any commission of inquiry or fact-finding mission to investigate the allegations of genocide.

The Government of Maldives condemns the ongoing attacks on Rafah by Israel Defence Forces and calls on Israel to abide by international human rights and humanitarian law and the measures ordered by the ICJ.

The Government of Maldives reaffirms that a lasting solution for the Palestinian people is through the establishment of an independent and sovereign state with pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

ENDS

en.title: Regarding the changes to the Sri Lankan Tourist Visa
en.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives wishes to clarify recent changes to Sri Lanka's tourist visa scheme.
en.body:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives wishes to clarify recent changes to Sri Lanka's tourist visa scheme.

Following the announcement of a new e-visa system in Sri Lanka, the Ministry has been engaged in discussions with Sri Lankan counterparts to ensure a smooth transition for Maldivian travellers.

The current procedure allows Maldivians to obtain a free 30-day tourist visa upon arrival in Sri Lanka. For stays exceeding 30 days, Maldivians can apply for a free 6-month visa online at <https://www.srilankaevisa.lk/>. This visa incurs an administrative fee.

For those Maldivians who are already in Sri Lanka and  require a visa extension may contact the Maldives High Commission in Colombo.

The Ministry is committed to establishing a visa process that reflects the current visa agreement between the Maldives and Sri Lanka and ensures reciprocity for Maldivian travellers. Discussions with Sri Lankan authorities are ongoing to address any remaining concerns.

Maldivians planning to visit Sri Lanka may contact the Ministry for any further assistance.

ENDS

en.title: Xizang Autonomous Region Donates Mineral Water
en.description: The Government of Maldives today received a donation of 1500 tonnes of mineral water as a kind gesture from the people of Xizang Autonomous Region of the People’s Republic of China.
en.body:
The Government of Maldives today received a donation of 1500 tonnes of mineral water as a kind gesture from the people of Xizang Autonomous Region of the People’s Republic of China.

At a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today, the donation was received by His Excellency Moosa Zameer, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives. The donation was handed over by Her Excellency Wang Lixin, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the Republic of Maldives.

The donation will be distributed to island communities, for use during times of drinking water shortage.

Speaking at the ceremony today, Foreign Minister Moosa Zameer highlighted on the warm relations between Maldives and China and mentioned that China continues to remain as a good friend of the Maldives, especially during challenging times and crisis.

Minister Zameer also expressed his gratitude to the people of Xijang Autonomous Region for the kind gesture and to the Government and the people of China for the continued support and goodwill extended to the people and the Government of Maldives.

ENDS.

en.title: Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Dr Ali Naseer Mohamed Presents Credentials to the United Nations Secretary-General
en.description: The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Dr Ali Naseer Mohamed presented his Letter of Credence to Secretary-General António Guterres today, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York.
en.body:
The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Dr Ali Naseer Mohamed presented his Letter of Credence to Secretary-General António Guterres today, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York.

During the ceremony, Ambassador Ali Naseer conveyed greetings and warm regards from President Dr Mohamed Muizzu to the Secretary-General and expressed the intention of the Government of Maldives to continue working closely with the United Nations.

Ambassador Ali Naseer was appointed by President Dr Mohamed Muizzu as the new Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations on 7th May 2024. Prior to his appointment, Ambassador Ali Naseer has been serving as Ambassador at Large of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Ambassador Ali Naseer headed the President-elect Muizzu’s Transition Committee on Foreign Relations until the President’s inauguration on 17 November 2023.

Ambassador Ali Naseer joined the Maldives Foreign Service in May 1985 and has served in various capacities in the service, both at the Headquarters and at Missions overseas. He held key positions including, Director-General for External Resources, Director-General for Political Affairs, Additional Secretary for Policy Planning, Foreign Secretary of the Maldives, Ambassador to the United States, Ambassador to Canada, Permanent Representative to the United Nations (2017-2019), and Secretary, Multilateral.

Ambassador Ali Naseer holds a PhD in International Relations from the Australian National University, MA from Leicester University, United Kingdom, and a Graduate Diploma in Business Administration from the University of Sydney, Australia.

END

dv.title: އެކުވެރި ދައުލަތްތަކުގެ ޖަމްޢިއްޔާއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު މުޙައްމަދު ފަތްކޮޅު އަރުވައިފި
dv.description: އެކުވެރި ދައުލަތްތަކުގެ ޖަމްޢިއްޔާއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު މުޙައްމަދު އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މަޤާމުގެ ފަތްކޮޅު އ.ދ.ގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ-ޖެނެރަލް އެންޓޯނިއޯ ގުޓެރެސް އަށް އަރުއްވައިފިއެވެ. ފަތްކޮޅު އެރުވުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތު ބާއްވާފައިވަނީ ނިއުޔޯކު ގައި…
dv.body:
އެކުވެރި ދައުލަތްތަކުގެ ޖަމްޢިއްޔާއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު ޑޮކްޓަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު މުޙައްމަދު އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މަޤާމުގެ ފަތްކޮޅު އ.ދ.ގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ-ޖެނެރަލް އެންޓޯނިއޯ ގުޓެރެސް އަށް އަރުއްވައިފިއެވެ. ފަތްކޮޅު އެރުވުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތު ބާއްވާފައިވަނީ ނިއުޔޯކު ގައި ހުންނަ އ.ދ. ގެ މައިމަރުކަޒުގައެވެ.

ފަތްކޮޅު އެރުވުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތަށްފަހު ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ވަނީ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒުގެ ފަރާތުން ސެކްރެޓަރީ-ޖެނެރަލަށް ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮއެދުން އަރިސްކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ. އާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އާއި ދެމެދު އޮތް ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކުރުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މަސައްކަތްކުރަމުންގެންދާނެ ކަމުގެ ޔަގީންކަން އެމަނިކުފާނު ސެކްރެޓެރީ-ޖެނެރަލަށް އެރުވިއެވެ.

އ.ދ. އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބުކަމަށް އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޢައްޔަނުކުރައްވައިފައިވަނީ 7 މޭ 2024 ގައެވެ. އެމަޤާމަށް އައްޔަން ކުރެއްވުމުގެ ކުރިން އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ހުންނެވީ ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގެ އެމްބެސެޑަރ އެޓް ލާޖްގެ މަޤާމުގައެވެ. އަދި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު 17 ނޮވެމްބަރ 2023 ގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ ހުވާކުރެއްވުމާ ހަމައަށް އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ހުންނެވީ އިންތިހާބީ ރައީސްގެ ޓްރާންޒިޝަން ކޮމިޓީގެ ޚާރިޖީ ގުޅުންތަކާބެހޭ ބައިގެ އިސްވެރިއެއްގެ ގޮތުގައެވެ.

1985ގެ މޭ މަހުން ފެށިގެން އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ވަނީ ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގެ އެކި މަގާމުތަކުގައި ޚިދުމަތްކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އެގޮތުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ވަނީ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ފޯ އެކްސްޓަރނަލް ރިސޯސަސް، ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ފޯ ޕޮލިޓިކަލް އެފެއާޒް، އެޑިޝަނަލް ސެކްރެޓަރީ ފޯ ޕޮލިސީ ޕްލޭނިންގ، ފޮރިން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ، އެމެރިކާއަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، ކެނެޑާއަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު، އ.ދ. އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބު (2017-2019)، އަދި ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓްރީގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ، މަލްޓިލޭޓަރަލްގެ ގޮތުގައި ޚިދުމަތް ކުރައްވާފައެވެ.

އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޢަލީ ނަޞީރު ވަނީ އޮސްޓްރޭލިއަން ނޭޝަނަލް ޔުނިވާސިޓީން އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް ރިލޭޝަންސްގެ ދާއިރާއިން ޕީއެޗްޑީ ހާސިލް ކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި އިނގިރޭސިވިލާތުގެ ލެސްޓާ ޔުނިވާސިޓީން އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް ރިލޭޝަންސްގެ ދާއިރާއިން މާސްޓާސް ޑިގްރީގެ އިތުރުން އޮސްޓްރޭލިއާގެ ސިޑްނީ ޔުނިވާސިޓީ އިން ބިޒްނަސް އެޑްމިނިސްޓްރޭޝަންގެ ދާއިރާއިން ގްރެޖުއޭޓް ޑިޕްލޮމާ ހާސިލް ކުރައްވާފައިވެއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer sends National Day greetings to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Cameroon
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of External Relations of the Republic of Cameroon, His Excellency Lejeune Mbella Mbella, on the occasion of Cameroon's National Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of External Relations of the Republic of Cameroon, His Excellency Lejeune Mbella Mbella, on the occasion of Cameroon's National Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, let me convey warm felicitations and sincere greetings to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of the Republic of Cameroon on the joyous occasion of your National Day.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs sends a message of condolence to the Vice President of Iran
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of condolence to the Vice President of the Islamic Republic of Iran His Excellency Mohammad Mokhber on the passing away of Iran’s President and Foreign Minister in the tragic helicopter crash…
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of condolence to the Vice President of the Islamic Republic of Iran His Excellency Mohammad Mokhber on the passing away of Iran’s President and Foreign Minister in the tragic helicopter crash in Iran’s East Azerbaijan Province.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of His Excellency Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi, President of the Islamic Republic of Iran and His Excellency Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the delegation accompanying the President, in the helicopter crash in Iran’s East Azerbaijan Province yesterday.

His Excellency Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi was a dedicated leader who will be remembered for his wisdom and unwavering commitment to the betterment of Iran and its people. His Excellency Hossein Amir-Abdollahian was a keen supporter of the renewed relationship between our two countries and we fondly remember his significant contributions to enhance the foreign policy of Iran.

At this time of profound grief and sorrow, I pray to Almighty Allah to bless President Raisi and Foreign Minister Amir-Abdollahian and the accompanying delegation and to grant them Jannatul Firdaus. The Government and people of Maldives join me in offering our most sincere condolences to the people of the Islamic Republic of Iran on this tragic loss. May the memories and legacy of His Excellency Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi and His Excellency Hossein Amir-Abdollahian continue to inspire generations to come.

“Surely to Allah we belong and surely to Him we shall return.”"

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives calls on the Security Council to re-consider the admission of Palestine in line with General Assembly Resolution
en.description: The Maldives called on the Security Council to re-consider the admission of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations in line with the Resolution “Admission of New Member States to the United Nations”, which was adopted by the General Assembly on Friday.
en.body:
The Maldives called on the Security Council to re-consider the admission of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations in line with the Resolution “Admission of New Member States to the United Nations”, which was adopted by the General Assembly on Friday.

During the statement delivered at the tenth Emergency Special Session, the Maldives noted that the overwhelming support for the Resolution sent a strong message to the Security Council. The Maldives further called on United Nations member states to act with urgency to stop the ongoing suffering in Palestine, and make Israel comply with its obligations under international law and international humanitarian law.

The Maldives further emphasised that a comprehensive solution to the conflict in the Middle East can only be achieved with the recognition and establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine, based on pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The tenth Emergency Special Session was resumed on 10 May 2024 upon the request of the Chairs of the Arab Group, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, and the Non-aligned Movement.

ENDS

dv.title: އ.ދ. ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީނު ބަލައިގަތުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އަނެއްކާވެސް ގޮވާލައިފި
dv.description: އދ.ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެންބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީން ބަލައިގަތުމަށް އދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އަނެއްކާވެސް ގޮވާލައިފިއެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މިހެން ގޮވާލާފައިވަނީ އދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުން މިދިޔަ ހުކުރު ދުވަހު "އެޑްމިޝަން އޮފް ނިއު މެންބަރ ސްޓޭޓްސް ޓު ދަ ޔުނައިޓެޑް ނޭޝަންސް" ގެ…
dv.body:
އދ.ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެންބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީން ބަލައިގަތުމަށް އދ.ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އަނެއްކާވެސް ގޮވާލައިފިއެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މިހެން ގޮވާލާފައިވަނީ އދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުން މިދިޔަ ހުކުރު ދުވަހު "އެޑްމިޝަން އޮފް ނިއު މެންބަރ ސްޓޭޓްސް ޓު ދަ ޔުނައިޓެޑް ނޭޝަންސް" ގެ ނަމުގައި ފާސްކޮށްފައިވާ ޤަރާރާށް ނިސްބަތްކޮށް، އ.ދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގެ 10 ވަނަ ކުއްލި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައެވެ.

މިބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ވަނީ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުން ފާސްކުރި ޤަރާރަށް މެންބަރު ޤައުމުތަކުން ލިބުނު ތާޢީދަކީ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ފޮނުވުނު ވަރުގަދަ މެސެޖެއް ގެ ގޮތުގައި ސިފަކޮށްފައެވެ. އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ވަނީ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުން ކުރިމަތިލާންޖެހިފައިވާ ހިތްދަތިކަމާއި ތަހައްމަލުކުރަމުންދާ އަނިޔާތައް ހުއްޓުމަށް އަވަސް ފިޔަވަޅުއެޅުމަށާއި، އިސްރާއީލުން ކުރަމުންދާ ޢަމަލުތަކަށް އެޤައުމު ޖަވާބުދާރީކުރުމަށް އ.ދ. ގެ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމުތަކަށް ގޮވާލާފައެވެ.

މެދުއިރުމަތީގެ ހަމަނުޖެހުންތަކަށް ދާއިމީ ހައްލެއް ގެނައުމަށް އޮތް ހަމައެކަނި ގޮތަކީ، 1967 ގެ ކުރިން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ބޯޑަރުތަކާ އެއްގޮތްވާ ގޮތުގެމަތިން، އިރުމަތީ ޤުދުސް އަކީ އެ ޤައުމުގެ ވެރިކަންކުރާ ރަށް ކަމަށް ކަނޑައަޅާ، ފަލަސްތީންގައި މިނިވަން ދައުލަތެއް ގާއިމުކުރުން ކަމަށްވެސް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ބަޔާނުގައި ތަކުރާރުކޮށްފައިވެއެވެ.

އ.ދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގެ 10 ވަނަ ކުއްލި ބައްދަލުވުން މިދިޔަ ހުކުރުދުވަހު އަލުން ހުޅުވާލާފައިވަނީ އަރަބް ގްރޫޕް، އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން އަދި ނޮން-އެލައިންޑް މޫވްމަންޓް އިން އެދިގެންނެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer concludes his Official Visit to Qatar
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer has concluded his Official Visit to Qatar from 11-13 May 2024. The visit aimed to enhance bilateral ties between the Maldives and Qatar.

en.title: Government of India extends budget support to the Government of Maldives
en.description: The Government India has provided a budget support of USD 50 million to the Maldives today. The support was in the form of a rollover of USD 50 million Treasury Bill, for an additional year, through the State Bank of India, Male’, from 13 May 2024.
en.body:
The Government India has provided a budget support of USD 50 million to the Maldives today. The support was in the form of a rollover of USD 50 million Treasury Bill, for an additional year, through the State Bank of India, Male’, from 13 May 2024.

Government of India’s decision to rollover the T-Bill came following a request to that effect made by Foreign Minister Moosa Zameer to India’s External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar, during the official bilateral visit to India from 8-10 May 2024.

The Government of Maldives is highly appreciative of the generous support that Government of India has been providing to the Maldives in the form of budgetary support. Large number of infrastructural developmental projects and High Impact Community Developmental projects are underway with the assistance from the Government of India, which consists of a notable part as grant assistance.

The Government of Maldives looks forward in continuing this collaborative partnership for the mutual benefit and prosperity of their people.

ENDS

en.title: Minister of State for Foreign Affairs meets Minister of State for the Indo-Pacific of UK
en.description: Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Sheryna Abdul Samad, met The Rt. Hon. Anne-Marie Trevelyan MP, Minister of State for the Indo-Pacific of United Kingdom of Great Britain, and Northern Ireland today.
en.body:
Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Sheryna Abdul Samad, met The Rt. Hon. Anne-Marie Trevelyan MP, Minister of State for the Indo-Pacific of United Kingdom of Great Britain, and Northern Ireland today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Sheryna warmly welcomed Minister Trevelyan to the Maldives, who was on her first official visit to the country. State Minister Sheryna noted that Minister Trevelyan’s visit signifies the importance the government of the United Kingdom attaches to strengthening the longstanding relations with Maldives. Minister Trevelyan assured that she wishes to enhance the existing cooperation on several areas of mutual interest and looks forward to exploring further opportunities with the new administration of President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu.

State Minister Sheryna further welcomed the United Kingdom’s decision to pursue a Free Trade Agreement with the Maldives, which will help to reduce the tariff barrier for fish exports to the United Kingdom from Maldives. Both Ministers also discussed having the second round of strategic dialogue between Maldives and United Kingdom in London later this year. Further discussions between the Ministers included enhancing bilateral relations across multiple sectors, including counterterrorism, maritime security, tourism, higher education, climate change and trade.

Minister Sheryna also expressed concerns on the grave human rights and humanitarian situation in Gaza and reiterated the Maldives’ firm call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire.

Minister Trevelyan arrived in the Maldives on 9 May 2024 and was received by Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed. During the visit, Minister Trevelyan held talks with Vice President Uz. Hussain Mohamed Latheef, Minister of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, Thoriq Ibrahim, Minister of Homeland Security and Technology, Ali Ihusaan, and Minister of Economic Development and Trade, Mohamed Saeed.

ENDS.

During the meeting, Minister Zameer reflected on the growing Maldives - Qatar partnership and thanked Qatar for the generous assistance in our socio-economic development. The two Ministers reiterated the commitment to deepen bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

Minister Zameer also conveyed appreciation for Qatar’s role in the mediation process on the Gaza crisis. The two Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen the partnership in the multilateral fora on matters of global concern.

Minister Zameer was accompanied at the meeting by Secretary, Bilateral, Dr Hala Hameed, Ambassador-at-Large, Dr Fazeel Najeeb, and Assistant Director, Lamha Saleem.

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives co-sponsors Resolution to admit the State of Palestine as a full member of the United Nations
en.description: The Maldives co-sponsored the resolution to support the admission of the State of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations which was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly today. The resolution was presented by the United Arab Emirates on behalf of the Arab Group, and the…
en.body:
The Maldives co-sponsored the resolution to support the admission of the State of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations which was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly today. The resolution was presented by the United Arab Emirates on behalf of the Arab Group, and the Maldives was among the first states to co-sponsor the draft resolution.

The Resolution entitled ‘Admission of new members to the United nations’ was considered following the resumption of the tenth Emergency Special Session. The Resolution determines that the State of Palestine is qualified for membership in the United Nations and recommends the Security Council to consider the matter favourably. The resolution further decides that Palestine shall be given additional rights of participation within the United Nations system, starting from the seventy-ninth session of the General Assembly.

The Resolution was passed by the General Assembly with 143 votes in favour, 9 against, and 25 abstentions.

dv.title: އ.ދ. ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީނު ބަލައިގަތުމަށް ބާރުއަޅާ ގަރާރު ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކޯ-ސްޕޮންސަރ ކޮށްފި
dv.description: އދ.ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެންބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީން ބަލައިގަތުމަށް އދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުން މިއަދު ފާސްކުރި ޤަރާރު ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކޯ-ސްޕޮންސަރ ކޮށްފިއެވެ. އެކުވެރި ޢަރަބި އިމާރާތުން ހުށަހެޅި މިޤަރާރު ކޯ-ސްޕޮންސަރކުރި އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ހިމެނެއެވެ. މި ޤަރާރުގައި…
dv.body:
އދ.ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެންބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީން ބަލައިގަތުމަށް އދ.ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުން މިއަދު ފާސްކުރި ޤަރާރު ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކޯ-ސްޕޮންސަރ ކޮށްފިއެވެ. އެކުވެރި ޢަރަބި އިމާރާތުން ހުށަހެޅި މިޤަރާރު ކޯ-ސްޕޮންސަރކުރި އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ހިމެނެއެވެ.

މި ޤަރާރުގައި ވަނީ އ.ދ. ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމަކަށް ވުމުގެ ޝަރުތުތައް ފަލަސްތީނުން ފުރިހަމަކޮށްފައިވާކަން ފާހަގަ ކޮށް، ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހުން އ.ދ. ގެ ފުރިހަމަ މެމްބަރު ޤައުމެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ފަލަސްތީނު ބަލައިގަތުމަށް ގޮވާލާފައެވެ. އަދި އ.ދ.ގެ ޢާއްމު މަޖިލީހުގެ 79ވަނަ ސެޝަނުން ފެށިގެން އ.ދ.ގެ ނިޒާމުގައި ބައިވެރިވުމުގައި މިހާރަށް ވުރެ އިތުރު ޙައްޤުތަކެއް ފަލަސްތީނަށް ދިނުމަށް ވެސް މިޤަރާރުން ވަނީ ފާސްކޮށްފައެވެ.

މި ޤަރާރު ފާސްކޮށްފައިވަނީ ވޯޓުގައި ބައިވެރިވި ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން 143 ޤައުމުގެ ތާއީދާއެކުގައެވެ. މިޤަރާރާ ދެކޮޅަށް 9 ޤައުމުން ވޯޓުދީފައިވާއިރު 25 ޤައުމަކުން ވަކިކޮޅަކަށް ވޯޓުދޭން ބޭނުންނުވާކަމަށް ވަނީ ކަނޑައަޅާފައެވެ.

en.title: Dr. Salma Rasheed Presents Her Credentials as Permanent Representative of Maldives to the Director-General of the United Nations Office at Geneva
en.description: Dr. Salma Rasheed, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, has officially presented her Letter of Credence to the Director General of the United Nations Office at Geneva, Tatiana Valovaya, in a formal ceremony held at the Palais des Nations today.
en.body:
Dr. Salma Rasheed, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, has officially presented her Letter of Credence to the Director General of the United Nations Office at Geneva, Tatiana Valovaya, in a formal ceremony held at the Palais des Nations today.

During the ceremony, Ambassador Dr. Salma extended her gratitude to Director General Valovaya for the warm reception and relayed greetings from President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu, the Government, and the people of Maldives to the UN Secretary-General, H.E. Mr. António Guterres.

She also expressed the President's appreciation for his leadership and the impactful work of the UN in these challenging times. Ambassador Dr. Salma reaffirmed the dedication and commitment of the Government of Maldives to promote and protect human rights and fundamental freedoms, as well as making significant contributions toward achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and the 2030 Agenda.

Ambassador Dr. Salma also thanked the Director General for emphasizing gender parity, climate change, and international economic integration as her priorities, and for her continued advocacy for geographical representation in the United Nations Office in Geneva. She further shared President Muizzu’s foreign policy priorities on climate change, democracy, good governance, rule of law, human rights, and gender equality, and reassured the commitment of the Maldives to remain a leading voice for Small Island Developing States.

President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu appointed Dr. Salma Rasheed as the new Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations in Geneva on 7th May 2024. Dr. Salma brings a wealth of experience from over 40 years in the health sector, notably for her roles in developing the first National Health Plan and the national childhood immunization program in the Maldives. She holds a PhD in Evaluation from London South Bank University, with further academic credentials from Leeds University and the American University of Beirut.

In her 17-year extensive career with the United Nations, including roles with UNFPA and WHO, Dr. Salma served in various leadership positions such as Deputy Representative and Regional Advisor, contributing to health system advancements in several countries across Asia and Africa.

dv.title: ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ރަޝީދު ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަވާ އެކުވެރި ދައުލަތްތަކުގެ މަރުކަޒުތަކުގެ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލްއަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބުކަމުގެ ފަތްކޮޅު އަރުވައިފި
dv.description: ޕެލޭ ޑި ނޭޝަންސްގައި މިއަދު ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އ.ދ.ގެ މަރުކަޒުތަކުގެ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ޓަޓިއާނާ ވަލޮވާޔާއަށް، ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ރަޝީދު، އެކަމަނާގެ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބުކަމަގެ ފަތްކޮޅު ރަސްމީކޮށް އަރުއްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
ޕެލޭ ޑި ނޭޝަންސްގައި މިއަދު ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އ.ދ.ގެ މަރުކަޒުތަކުގެ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ޓަޓިއާނާ ވަލޮވާޔާއަށް، ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ރަޝީދު، އެކަމަނާގެ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބުކަމަގެ ފަތްކޮޅު ރަސްމީކޮށް އަރުއްވައިފިއެވެ.

މި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ޑރ. ސަލްމާއަށް މަރުޙަބާ ދެންނެވިކަމަށްޓަކައި ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ވަލޮވާޔާއަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާ، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު އާއި، ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި، ރައްޔިތުންގެ ފަރާތުން އދ.ގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލް އެންޓޯނިއޯ ގުޓަރޭޒްއަށް ތަހުނިޔާ ފޮނުއްވިއެވެ.

އަދި ދުނިޔޭގެ މަޝްރަޙު ހަލަބޮލިވެފައިވާ މިފަދަ ދަނޑިވަޅެއްގައި އ.ދ.ގެ އިސްނެގުމާއި ކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ މަސައްކަތްތަކަށް އެކަމަނާ ވަނީ ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާއި އަސާސީ މިނިވަންކަން ކުރިއަރުވާ ޙިމާޔަތްކުރުމަށާއި، ދެމެހެއްޓެނިވި ތަރައްޤީގެ ލަނޑުދަނޑިތަކާއި 2030 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ އެޖެންޑާ ޙާޞިލުކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ކުރެވޭ މަސައްކަތުގައި ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ބައިވެރިވާނެކަމުގެ ފުރިހަމަ ޔަޤީންކަން ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ވަނީ ދެއްވާފައެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން، ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ވަނީ ގިންތީގެ ހަމަހަމަކަން ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށާއި، މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުން ކުރާ ނޭދެވޭ އަސަރުތަކަށް ހައްލު ހޯދާ ދިނުމަށާއި، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ އިޤްތިޞާދީ އެއްބައިވަންތަކަން އަލާކުރުމަށާއި، ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އދ.ގެ މަރުކަޒުތަކުގައި ދުނިޔޭގެ އެކި ސަރަހައްދުތަކުގެ ޤައުމުތައް ތަމްސީލުކުރުމުގައި ހަމަހަމަކަން ގެންގުޅުމަށް ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޖެނެރަލް ކުރައްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ މަސައްކަތް ފާހަގަކޮށް އެކަމަނާއަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތުގައި މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކާއި، ޑިމޮކްރަސީއާއި، ހެޔޮވެރިކަމާއި، ޤާނޫނީ ވެރިކަމާއި، އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތަކާއި، ގިންތީގެ ހަމަހަމަކަމަށް އިސްކަންދޭ މިންވަރު ހާމަކޮށް، ތަރައްޤީވަމުން އަންނަ ކުދި ޖަޒީރާ ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ޙައްޤުތަކަށް ވަކާލާތުކުރުމުގައި އިސް ދައުރެއް އަދާކުރުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ދެމި އޮންނާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ދެއްވިއެވެ.

ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު މުޢިއްޒު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ޖެނީވާގައި ހުންނަ އދ. ގެ ދާއިމީ މިޝަން އަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައި ހުންނަވާ ދާއިމީ މަންދޫބުގެ މަޤާމަށް ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ރަޝީދު ޢައްޔަން ކުރެއްވީ 7 މެއި 2024 ގައެވެ. ސިއްހީ ދާއިރާގައި 40 އަހަރަށް ވުރެ ގިނަ އަހަރުގެ ތަޖުރިބާ ހޯއްދަވާފައިވާ ޑރ. ސަލްމާ އަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި އެންމެ ފުރަތަމަ ނެޝަނަލް ހެލްތު ޕްލޭންއާއި ނެޝަނަލް އިމިއުނައިޒޭޝަން ޕްރޮގްރާމް އެކުލަވާލުމުގައި އިސް ދައުރެއް އަދާކުރެއްވި ބޭފުޅެކެވެ. ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ވަނީ ލަންޑަން ސައުތު ބޭންކް ޔުނިވާސިޓީ އިން އިވެލުއޭޝަންގެ ދާއިރާއިން ޕީއެޗްޑީ ހާސިލްކުރައްވާފައެވެ. އަދި، އެކަމަނާ ވަނީ ލީޑްސް ޔުނިވާސިޓީ އާއި އެމެރިކަން ޔުނިވާސިޓީ އޮފް ބެއިރޫތު އިން މަތީ ތައުލީމީ ސަނަދުތަކެއް ހާސިލްކުރައްވާފައެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން، ޔޫ.އެން.އެފް.ޕީ.އޭ. އާއި ޑަބްލިއު.އެޗް.އޯ.އާ. އެކު މަސައްކަތްކުރެއްވި 17 އަހަރުގެ ދިގު ކެރިއަރުގައި ޑރ. ސަލްމާ ވަނީ ޑެޕިއުޓީ ރެޕްރެޒެންޓޭޓިވް އަދި ރީޖަނަލް އެޑްވައިޒަރު ފަދަ އެކިއެކި އިސް މަޤާމުތައް ފުރުއްވާފައެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer arrives after concluding his Official Visit to India
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Moosa Zameer concluded his first official bilateral visit to India.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Moosa Zameer concluded his first official bilateral visit to India.

During the visit, Minister of Foreign Affairs met with the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar and held bilateral talks and reviewed the long standing partnership for enhancing cooperation.

Minister Zameer also visited the High Commission of Maldives in India and met with the staff. At a separate event, Minister also interacted with the Maldivian community visiting and residing in New Delhi.

Minister also engaged with Indian media and spoke about the Maldives-India partnership, the future prospects of the cooperation.

ENDs

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer and Minister of External Affairs, Dr. S. Jaishankar hold official talks
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, held official talks with Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar, today. Both sides engaged in discussions on all aspects of the partnership to forge opportunities for future collaboration in government priority areas. Both…
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, held official talks with Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar, today. Both sides engaged in discussions on all aspects of the partnership to forge opportunities for future collaboration in government priority areas. Both Ministers expressed commitment to continue working closely together, bilaterally and in international arena, on priority areas of mutual interest.

During the official discussions, both Ministers acknowledged the fruitful economic partnership and the notable progress of projects facilitated through Indian grant assistance and line of credit initiatives.

The dialogue comprised perspectives on development cooperation, tourism initiatives, and human resource development, underscoring a partnership built on mutual trusts shared interests and values.

Both Ministers also underscored the significance of exploring additional avenues to enhance the Maldives-India partnership.

 Minister Zameer conveyed appreciation for India’s steadfast support in fostering and advancing economic, trade, and investment ties between the two nations, as well as for India's committed role in the socioeconomic advancement of the Maldives. India had renewed quota for Maldives to import essential goods for one year amounting a significant increase compared to previous year.

Minister Zameer's first official visit to India reflects the strong support and commitment between the two countries. It marks a new initiative of collaboration, symbolizing enduring friendship and shared goals.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Europe Day greetings to the people and leadership of the European Union
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends a message of felicitations to His Excellency Josep Borrell Fontelles, High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs on the occasion of Europe Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends a message of felicitations to His Excellency Josep Borrell Fontelles, High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs on the occasion of Europe Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, it is with great pleasure that we offer our sincere felicitations to Your Excellency, as well as the leadership and people of the European Union on Europe Day.

The enduring relationship between the European Union (EU) and the Maldives celebrates its 41st anniversary of diplomatic ties this year. The EU has consistently stood as a steadfast partner in the Maldives’ democratic journey, making significant contributions to our nation’s progress and development. The Maldives continues to benefit from development initiatives by EU, especially on good governance and green recovery.  We therefore look forward to enhancing and broadening this existing partnership with EU.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and the assurances of my highest consideration.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Moosa Zameer to undertake an Official Visit to India
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Moosa Zameer will undertake an Official Visit to India from 8 to 10 May 2024.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Moosa Zameer will undertake an Official Visit to India from 8 to 10 May 2024.

During the visit, Minister Zameer will meet with India’s Minister of External Affairs Dr S. Jaishankar and hold discussions in deepening and expanding the longstanding partnership between the Maldives and India.

This is Foreign Minister Zameer's first official visit to India since assuming office.

en.title: The Fourth Meeting of the High-level Core Group between the Maldives and India
en.description: The Fourth Meeting of the High-level Core Group between the Maldives and India took place today (3 May 2024), in New Delhi. During the discussions held at MEA, both sides reviewed the existing bilateral cooperation. Discussions were held on a wide range of issues of mutual interest, including…
en.body:
The Fourth Meeting of the High-level Core Group between the Maldives and India took place today (3 May 2024), in New Delhi. During the discussions held at MEA, both sides reviewed the existing bilateral cooperation. Discussions were held on a wide range of issues of mutual interest, including development and defence cooperation.

Both sides noted with satisfaction that the Government of India will replace military personnel at the last of the three aviation platforms by 10 May and all the logistical arrangements are going ahead as per schedule.

It was further agreed that the fifth  meeting of the High-Level core Group will be held in Male’ on a mutually agreeable date during the month of June/July.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Constitution Day greetings to the Foreign Minister of Poland
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Radosław Sikorski, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Poland, on the occasion of the Constitution Day of Poland.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Radosław Sikorski, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Poland, on the occasion of the Constitution Day of Poland.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government, and the people of the Republic of Maldives, I would like to extend warm greetings and best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Poland, on the occasion of your Constitution Day.

I am confident that the friendly ties between our two countries will continue to prosper and flourish in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress and prosperity for the people of Poland and the assurances of my highest consideration”

en.title: Minister Zameer meets with the Director General of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development, Mohammed Saif Al Suwaidi
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, met with the Director General of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD), Mohammed Saif Al Suwaidi, in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, today.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, met with the Director General of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD), Mohammed Saif Al Suwaidi, in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, today.

During the meeting, Minister Zameer reflected on the long-standing bonds of friendship and cooperation between the Maldives and the UAE and expressed gratitude for the closeness accorded to the Maldives by the Government of the UAE.

Minister Zameer highlighted the generous assistance and consistent support provided by ADFD for the implementation of the projects and explored avenues to go forward with the proposals submitted to the Fund.

In particular, Minister Zameer expressed gratitude for the support towards the extension of Velana International Airport, noting that it will expand connectivity, leading to increased tourist arrivals and strengthening the resilience of the economy of the Maldives. He also highlighted the development of Maafaru International Airport project, including the expansion of the airport, would result in the realization of even more avenues for investment cooperation.

Minister Zameer was accompanied at the meeting by the Additional Secretary of the Ministry, Shiruzimath Sameer, the Deputy Ambassador of the Embassy of the Maldives in Abu Dhabi, Hassaan Waheed, and the Counsellor of the Embassy of the Maldives in Abu Dhabi, Moomina Ibrahim.

ENDS

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Kalani Kaneko, Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade of the Marshall Islands, on the occasion of the Constitution Day of Marshall Islands.

As fellow Small Island Developing States (SIDS), cooperation at the bilateral and multilateral level between our countries remain strong and we are committed to continue to advance our joint efforts to address shared challenges.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress and prosperity for the people of the Marshall Islands and the assurances of my highest consideration”

en.title: Maldives to Participate in the 46th Session of the UPR Working Group
en.description: The 46th Session of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) commenced at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, today. The session will continue for a period of two weeks and will conclude on 10 May 2024. During this Session, fourteen States will undergo the review of their respective human rights records.…
en.body:
The 46th Session of the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) commenced at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, today. The session will continue for a period of two weeks and will conclude on 10 May 2024. During this Session, fourteen States will undergo the review of their respective human rights records. The countries to be reviewed are Afghanistan, Chile, Cambodia, Comoros, Cyprus, Dominican Republic, Eritrea, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Slovakia, Uruguay, Vanuatu, Viet Nam and Yemen.

The UPR Working Group holds three sessions annually. The Fourth Cycle review of the UPR began in November 2022 and will conclude in 2027. The UPR is a State-driven process which involves a review of the overall situation of human rights of all UN Member States. This UN mechanism provides the States under review with the opportunity to declare the progress made in fulfilling their human rights obligations and commitments in their respective countries. It also allows fellow Member States to provide constructive recommendations on how the States under review can further improve the implementation of their human rights obligations. Each State review is further facilitated by groups of three States, known as “troikas”, who serve as rapporteurs. The Maldives as a member of the Human Rights Council has been selected to be represented in the Troika for the review of Yemen.

The Maldives delegation for the 46th Session of the UPR will be led by Dr. Salma Rasheed, Chargé d’affaires at the Permanent Mission of Maldives to the United Nations Office and other International Organisations in Geneva and will be accompanied by Counsellor Mr. Adam Hamid, Counsellor Uza. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, Second Secretary Ms. Maryam Fathika Fayaz, and Attaché Mr. Raaidh Saeedh, from the Permanent Mission. In line with the Government’s key policies and priorities, the Maldives delegation will actively engage and provide constructive recommendations during this UPR Session.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Zameer participates in the IGWEL High-Level Luncheon in the World Economic Forum Special Meeting on Global Collaboration, Growth and Energy for Development
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, participated in the Informal Gathering of World Economic Leaders (IGWEL) High-level Luncheon on “Charting a Global Security and Growth Agenda” during the World Economic Forum Special Meeting on Global Collaboration, Growth and Energy for Development…
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, participated in the Informal Gathering of World Economic Leaders (IGWEL) High-level Luncheon on “Charting a Global Security and Growth Agenda” during the World Economic Forum Special Meeting on Global Collaboration, Growth and Energy for Development today.

The High-level Luncheon brought together approximately 80 policy makers, business leaders and experts from different sectors to discuss and exchange views on addressing global security challenges faced by the world today.

Informal Gathering of World Economic Leaders (IGWEL) sessions are the World Economic Forum’s highest-level sessions and participation is by invitation only.

ENDS

dv.title: ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމްގެ އައި.ޖީ.ޑަބްލިއު.އީ.އެލް. ހައި-ލެވެލް ލަންޗަން ގައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންފި
dv.description: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު 'ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމް ސްޕެޝަލް މީޓިން އޮން ގްލޯބަލް ކޮލަބޮރޭޝަން، ގްރޯތް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް' ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ތެރެއިން "އިންފޯމަލް ގެދަރިންގ އޮފް ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ލީޑަރސް (އައި.ޖީ.ޑަބްލިއު.އީ.އެލް.) 'ޗަރޓިން އަ ގްލޯބަލް ސެކިއުރިޓީ ގްރޯތް އެޖެންޑާ' ގެ…
dv.body:
ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު 'ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމް ސްޕެޝަލް މީޓިން އޮން ގްލޯބަލް ކޮލަބޮރޭޝަން، ގްރޯތް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް' ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ތެރެއިން "އިންފޯމަލް ގެދަރިންގ އޮފް ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ލީޑަރސް (އައި.ޖީ.ޑަބްލިއު.އީ.އެލް.) 'ޗަރޓިން އަ ގްލޯބަލް ސެކިއުރިޓީ ގްރޯތް އެޖެންޑާ' ގެ ޝިއާރުގެ ދަށުން މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާ އިސްވެރިންނަށް ހާއްސަކޮށް ބޭއްވި "އިންފޯމަލް ގެދަރިންގ އޮފް ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ލީޑަރސް (އައި.ޖީ.ޑަބްލިއު.އީ.އެލް.) ހައި ލެވެލް ލަންޗަން" ގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އެކި ޤައުމުތަކުގެ އިސްވެރިންނާއި ވަޒީރުންނާއި ވިޔަފާރިވެރިންނާއި އެކި ދާއިރާތަކުގެ ތަޖުރިބާކާރުން ހިމެނޭ 80 ބޭފުޅުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތެވެ. އަދި މިއަދު ދުނިޔެއަށް ކުރިމަތިވެފައިވާ ސަލާމަތީ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކާ ކުރިމަތިލުމާ ގުޅޭ ގޮތުންނާއި، މެދުއިރުމަތީގައި ހިނގަމުންދާ ކަންކަމާއި އިސްރާއިލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާ ދެކޮޅަށް ދެމުންދާ ހަމަލާތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކޮށް ޚިޔާލު ބަދަލުކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމްގ އައި.ޖީ.ޑަބްލިއު.އީ.އެލް. ބައްދަލުވުންތަކަކީ މި ފޯރަމްގެ ބައިވެރިންގެ ތެރެއިން އެންމެ މަތީ ފަންތީގެ ބޭފުޅުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާ ބައްދަލުވުންތަކެވެ.

dv.title: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ރިޔާދަށް ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފި
dv.description: އޭޕްރިލް މަހުގެ 28 އިން 29 އަށް ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ 'ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމްގެ ސްޕެޝަލް މީޓިންގ އޮން ގްލޯބަލް ކޮލަބޮރޭޝަން، ގްރޯތް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީ ފޯރ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް' ގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށްޓަކައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ރިޔާދުއަށް މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
އޭޕްރިލް މަހުގެ 28 އިން 29 އަށް ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ 'ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމްގެ ސްޕެޝަލް މީޓިންގ އޮން ގްލޯބަލް ކޮލަބޮރޭޝަން، ގްރޯތް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީ ފޯރ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް' ގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށްޓަކައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ރިޔާދުއަށް މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ތެރެއިން ދުނިޔޭގެ އެކި ޤައުމުތަކުގެ މެދުގައި ގުޅުން ބަދަހިކުރުމުގެ މަޤްސަދުގައި ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ހައިލެވެލް ބައްދަލުވުންތަކުގައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޒަމީރު ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން ދުނިޔޭގެ އެކި ޤައުމުތަކުގެ ވެރިން، ބައިނަލްއަގްވާމީ ޖަމުޢިއްޔާތަކުގެ އިސްވެރިން، ވިޔާފާރީގެ ތަޖުރިބާކާރުންނާ ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ފުރުސަތު މި ބައްދަލުވުން މެދުވެރިކޮށް ލިބިގެންދާނެއެވެ.

'ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމްގެ ސްޕެޝަލް މީޓިންގ އޮން ގްލޯބަލް ކޮލަބޮރޭޝަން، ގްރޯތް އެންޑް އެނަރޖީ ފޯރ ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް' އަކީ ސައުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ސަރުކާރުން އާއި ވަރލްޑް އިކޮނޮމިކް ފޯރަމް އާ ގުޅިގެން ބާއްވާ ބައްދަލުވުމެކެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އެކި ދާއިރާތަކުގައި މަސައްކަތްކުރާ 700 އިސް ވެރިންނާއި ތަޖުރިބާ ކާރުން ބައިވެރިވެ ދުނިޔެއަށް ދިމާވެފައިވާ މުހިންމު ގޮންޖެހުންތަކަށް ހައްލު ހޯދުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރާނެއެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends a message of condolence to Wang Yi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the People’s Republic of China, following the multiple days of heavy rains that lashed onto southern China.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I am deeply saddened to learn of the devastating floods that have struck southern China, particularly in Guangdong province, affecting millions of lives and resulting in tragic loss of life and displacement of numerous individuals.

On behalf of the Government and people of the Maldives I extend our heartfelt sympathies to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of China during this challenging time. Our thoughts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones and those who have been affected by the floods.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Secretary, Economic and Development Cooperation Dr. Hussain Niyaaz leads the Maldives delegation to the 80th Session of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP)
en.description: The 80th Session of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and Pacific (ESCAP) commenced today in Bangkok. The Maldives delegation at the 80th Commission Session is led by Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary, Economic and Development Cooperation. The session will be held from 22-26 April 2024 at the…
en.body:
The 80th Session of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and Pacific (ESCAP) commenced today in Bangkok. The Maldives delegation at the 80th Commission Session is led by Dr. Hussain Niyaaz, Secretary, Economic and Development Cooperation. The session will be held from 22-26 April 2024 at the United Nations Conference Centre in Bangkok, Thailand.

The theme for the 80th Commission Session is  “Leveraging digital innovation for sustainable development in Asia and the Pacific” and provides an opportunity to strengthen region-wide cooperative action on leveraging digital innovation for the accelerated implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

In his remarks, Secretary, Economic and Development Cooperation highlighted the ambitious development agenda of the Government of Maldives which stems from innovation, sustainability and inclusivity. This includes the plans to establish smart and resilient urban centers throughout the Maldives, the "Ras Malé Eco-City project, the prioritization of e-government platforms and the utilization of artificial intelligence across various services.

Secretary, Economic Cooperation will also participate in a side event co-hosted by Maldives with Indonesia, Fiji and France entitled “Accelerating Ocean-Based Climate Action” held on the sidelines of the Session.

This year’s Session follows a thematic study undertaken by UNESCAP, which examines existing digital innovations that have accelerated progress towards sustainable development and explores ways to build on their successes. Delegations from ESCAP member countries and associate members, as well as independent organizations, are participating in the Commission Session.

Secretary, Economic, and Development Cooperation Dr. Hussain Niyaaz is accompanied by Ms. Aishath Shiruma Ahmed, First Secretary, Ms. Aishath Shahula, First Secretary and Ms. Siyana Shiyam, Second Secretary at the Embassy of the Republic of Maldives in the Kingdom of Thailand.

ENDS

en.title: The Maldives calls on the United Nations to admit the State of Palestine as a full member
en.description: The Maldives has called the United Nations Security Council to support the admission of the State of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations. The Maldives rendered its support during a statement delivered today by Principal Secretary to the President on Foreign Relations Mohamed…
en.body:
The Maldives has called the United Nations Security Council to support the admission of the State of Palestine as a full member state of the United Nations. The Maldives rendered its support during a statement delivered today by Principal Secretary to the President on Foreign Relations Mohamed Naseer at the United Nations Security Council Quarterly Open Debate on the situation in the Middle East.

During the statement, Principal Secretary Naseer called on the members of the United Nations; especially the permanent members of the United Nations Security Council to give their full and unconditional support for the admission of the State of Palestine to the United Nations as a full member state.  The Maldives also called on the United Nations Security Council to impose sanctions, including an arms embargo on Israel for violating the Charter of the Council on multiple occasions.

The Maldives reiterated its support for a lasting solution to the conflict, through a two-state solution, with the establishment of an independent and sovereign Palestinian State based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The Quarterly Open Debate on the Situation in the Middle East is being convened during the Presidency of Malta in the United Nations Security Council. On 2 April 2024, the State of Palestine submitted a letter to the Secretary General of the United Nations requesting renewed consideration be given to the application of the State of Palestine for membership in the United Nations.

ENDS

en.title: Secretary, Bilateral, Dr Hala Hameed met with Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade First Assistant Secretary, Sarah Storey.
en.description: Secretary, Bilateral, Dr Hala Hameed met with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary for North and South Asia Division, Sarah Storey, today.
en.body:
Secretary, Bilateral, Dr Hala Hameed met with Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s First Assistant Secretary for North and South Asia Division, Sarah Storey, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today, both Secretary Bilateral Dr Hala and First Assistant Secretary Storey reflected on the renewed vigour of the partnership between the Maldives and Australia in the recent years, especially with establishment of a resident High Commission in the Maldives.

Discussions also focused on the different avenues of cooperation between the two countries including, climate change, people-to-people ties, defence, Indian Ocean security and Australia’s immense contribution to human resource development. Both further agreed to hold regular ‘Senior Officials Talks’ hereon, to continue to explore avenues to further enhance the bilateral and multilateral cooperation between the two countries.

First Assistant Secretary Storey was accompanied by the Australian High Commissioner in the Maldives, David Jessup, Deputy High Commissioner, Andrew Hodges and Political Research and Information Officer, Abdulla Rasheed.

Secretary Bilateral Dr Hala Hameed was accompanied by Senior Undersecretary Hassan Hussain Shihab, and Desk Officer Saifulla Waleed.

en.title: The 55th Session of the Human Rights Council concludes with the active participation and engagement of the Maldives Delegation
en.description: The 55th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council concluded in Geneva, Switzerland on 5 April 2024.
en.body:
The 55th Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council concluded in Geneva, Switzerland on 5 April 2024.

During the session, the Human Rights Council passed 34 resolutions and appointed 14 Special Procedures Mandate holders. The Maldives delegation contributed actively by delivering 30 national statements and co-sponsoring 17 resolutions covering a wide range of thematic areas that aligned with key government priorities. These key priorities included the provision of adequate housing as a component of the right to an adequate standard of living, establishing support systems that ensure the inclusivity of Persons with Disabilities and fulfilling of the rights of the child, and ensuring the right of the Palestinian People to Self-Determination. The Maldives delegation also supported thematic areas centering on inclusive social protection, guaranteeing the right to work, the right to non-discrimination. Further, the Maldives supported the decision to utilise remote participation modalities to facilitate hybrid meetings for the Human Rights Council to enhance participation for delegations with limited resources.

The Maldives co-sponsored 34 joint statements including statements by the Organization for Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and Non-Aligned Movement (NAM). Representing the group of Small Island Developing States (SIDS), the Maldives delivered a joint statement emphasizing the need for enhanced technical and financial assistance for capacity building for SIDS to participate in the work of the Council.

The Maldives also played a pivotal role in advocating for the protection of journalists and freedom of expression in Palestine, delivering a joint statement on behalf of several countries. This statement emphasized the vital need for protecting the right of journalists and ensuring freedom of expression and assembly in the Occupied Palestinian Territories. Furthermore, the Maldives demonstrated its strong commitment to the Palestinian cause, by co-sponsoring five joint statements particularly focusing on the suffering in Gaza. These statements covered various themes, including children, women and girls, persons with disabilities, and the destruction of housing and infrastructure. Importantly, the Maldives voted in favour of four resolutions concerning the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which demonstrates the Government’s unwavering support for the Palestinian struggle for self-determination.

The Maldives delegation was led by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sheryna Abdul Samad and was further accompanied by Chargé d’affaires of the Permanent Mission of Maldives to the United Nations Office and other International Organisations at Geneva, Dr. Salma Rasheed, Counsellor Adam Hamid, Counsellor Uza. Aminath Shifaya Ibrahim, First Secretary Fathimath Razana, Second Secretary Maryam Fathika Fayaz, Attaché Raaidh Saeedh, from the Permanent Mission and Chief Desk Officer Fathin Shoora Haleem from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS.

en.title: Four Exchange of Notes signed between Maldives and Japan
en.description: The Government of the Republic of Maldives and Government of Japan today signed four bilateral agreements, marking a significant step in strengthening existing ties between the two countries. The Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Moosa Zameer and the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives,…
en.body:
The Government of the Republic of Maldives and Government of Japan today signed four bilateral agreements, marking a significant step in strengthening existing ties between the two countries. The Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Moosa Zameer and the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Her Excellency Takeuchi Midori signed the four Exchange of Notes at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The four Exchange of Notes are as follows:

1) Exchange of Notes Provision of Customs Patrol Craft based on Economic Cooperation Grant Act of Japan.

2) Exchange of Notes for the grant of 260 Million Japanese Yen for implementation of the Project for the Enhancement of AbilIty in Maritime Safety and Security.

3) Exchange of Notes for the grant of 600 Million Japanese Yen for the Provision of Equipment towards Strengthening Maldives' National Response Capacity to High Frequent Natural Hazards through Community Empowerment to the National Disaster Management Authority, under the Economic and Social Development Programme

4) Exchange of Notes for the Grant of 56 Million Japanese Yen for the Provision of Equipment to support operations of patrol vessels to the Maldives Customs Service, under the Economic and Social Development Programme.

Minister Zameer conveyed his appreciation for Japan's ongoing support and underscored the significance of this collaboration in advancing the socio-economic development of the Maldives. He also highlighted the important role played by Japan as one of the key development partners, and reiterated Maldives’ commitment to further build upon the excellent diplomatic relations between Maldives and Japan.

The signing ceremony was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Maldives Customs Service, National Disaster Management Authority, and the Embassy of Japan in the Maldives.

ENDS

en.title: Australia’s Ambassador for Climate Change calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: Australia’s Ambassador for Climate Change, Kristin Tilley paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer today.
en.body:
Australia’s Ambassador for Climate Change, Kristin Tilley paid a courtesy call on the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Zameer and Ambassador Tilley discussed the pressing challenges faced by climate vulnerable Small Island Developing States (SIDS) like the Maldives and opportunities to collaborate with like-minded countries such as Australia.

Minister Zameer also briefed on the environmental and climate change policies of President Dr Muizzu’s government including the shift to 33% renewable energy and the plan to plant five million trees throughout the Maldives. Minister also underscored the importance of jointly addressing the current challenges faced by SIDS in accessing climate financing through international financial institutions.

Discussions also centred around deepening the existing relations with emphasis on strengthening cooperation in areas such as tourism and people-to-people ties.

Minister Zameer was accompanied at the meeting by Secretary, Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Secretary, Multilateral Ahmed Shiaan, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed and Desk Officer Saifulla Waleed.

en.title: Foreign Minister Zameer addresses the Third Summit for Democracy
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer addressed today at the ‘Third Summit for Democracy’ convened by the Government of the Republic of Korea, under the theme “Democracy for Future Generations”.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer addressed today at the ‘Third Summit for Democracy’ convened by the Government of the Republic of Korea, under the theme “Democracy for Future Generations”.

In his remarks, Foreign Minister Zameer highlighted the commitment of the Government of Maldives to uphold the principles of democracy, justice, and equality.

In particular, Minister Zameer underscored the efforts taken by President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu to nurture an independent civil society and, to ensure equal access to justice for all citizens. Additionally, Minister Zameer reflected on the Government’s initiatives on empowering youth and prioritizing women’s participation in the decision-making process and increasing women’s engagement in politics.

Minister Zameer also highlighted the fruitful collaboration between the Maldives and the United States in implementing reforms aimed at ensuring equal access to justice which led to the reorganization of the Maldivian court system.

Hosted by the President of South Korea Yoon Suk Yeol, the Third Summit for Democracy is being held in Seoul, South Korea from March 18th to 20th. Summit for Democracy is an initiative of the United States and was first launched in 2021.

en.body:

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, both sides noted the progress that have been made in replacing Indian military personnel with civilians at the aviation platforms in the Maldives. To date, military personnel in one such platform have been replaced with civilians, and the remaining two will be replaced by civilians on 10 April and 10 May 2024.

The High Level Core Group covered broad range of areas in economic and development cooperation between the two countries, and noted the capacity building programs recently concluded. Additionally, discussions covered areas related to bilateral cooperation aimed at enhancing the partnership, including expediting the implementation of ongoing developmental cooperation projects.

It was agreed that the Fourth meeting of the High-Level Core Group will be held in New Delhi on a mutually agreeable date.

en.title: Message by His Excellency Moosa Zameer, Minister of Foreign Affairs on the occasion of Commonwealth Day
en.description: “On this year’s Commonwealth Day, we join all Member States to celebrate the spirit of unity that brings us together as a family. This year also marks the 75th anniversary of the Commonwealth – a commitment that embraces diversity. A commitment that has triumphed over trial. A commitment that has…
en.body:
“On this year’s Commonwealth Day, we join all Member States to celebrate the spirit of unity that brings us together as a family. This year also marks the 75th anniversary of the Commonwealth – a commitment that embraces diversity. A commitment that has triumphed over trial. A commitment that has delivered results.

What makes us great are our common values, our common interests, and our resolve to rise to common challenges. These strengths are a proven path to a Commonwealth that, above all, perseveres. It has led us to a more prosperous and sustainable future.

Yet, common challenges, such as climate change, financing gaps, digital divide, and gender inequality remain. These forces have tested the most vulnerable among us. It has pushed Small Island Developing States (SIDS) like the Maldives further away from achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Addressing these challenges require solution-based approaches, partnerships, and a united effort. This is what the Commonwealth has been all about. It unites us in the face of threats. It voices our concerns and needs. It empowers the most vulnerable.

Guided by the Commonwealth Charter, and in the lead up to and beyond the Commonwealth Heads of the Government Meeting 2024, the Maldives is committed to unite for a resilient common future.

Happy Commonwealth Day!”

en.title: The Maldives Calls for Imposing an Immediate Arms Embargo on Israel
en.description: The Maldives has called for an immediate arms embargo to be imposed on Israel. The Maldives made this call in the statement delivered today by Chargé d'affaires Ambassador Dr Ali Naseer Mohamed at the Plenary Meeting of the United Nations General Assembly on the ‘Use of the veto’.
en.body:
The Maldives has called for an immediate arms embargo to be imposed on Israel. The Maldives made this call in the statement delivered today by Chargé d'affaires Ambassador Dr Ali Naseer Mohamed at the Plenary Meeting of the United Nations General Assembly on the ‘Use of the veto’.

In his statement, Chargé d'affaires Ambassador Mohamed stated that the latest veto in the United Nations Security Council on 20 February gave Israel a license to continue with impunity and kill more than a hundred Palestinian civilians and injure hundreds more during the incident of 29 February. The Maldives said that the civilians that Israel killed on that day and since then were those who had been deprived by Israel, of food, water, and other necessities.

Chargé d'affaires Ambassador Mohamed called on the Security Council to take immediate action to stop Israel’s ongoing genocide in Palestine. He urged the Council and the international community to move beyond rhetoric and take decisive action to halt Israel’s actions and hold it accountable for war crimes against the Palestinian people.

dv.title: އިސްރާއީލަށް ހަތިޔާރު ވިއްކުން މަނާ ކުރުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އ.ދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ގޮވާލައިފި
dv.description: އިސްރާއީލަށް ހަތިޔާރު ވިއްކުން މަނާ ކުރުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ގޮވާލައިފިއެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މިގޮތަށް ގޮވާލާފައިވަނީ، އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނާ ދެކޮޅަށް މިހާރު ކުރަމުން ގެންދާ ހަނގުރާމަ ވަގުތުން ހުއްޓާ ލުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން އ.ދ. އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ކުރިއަށްދިޔަ ބަހުސްގައި…
dv.body:
އިސްރާއީލަށް ހަތިޔާރު ވިއްކުން މަނާ ކުރުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން އދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ގޮވާލައިފިއެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން މިގޮތަށް ގޮވާލާފައިވަނީ، އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނާ ދެކޮޅަށް މިހާރު ކުރަމުން ގެންދާ ހަނގުރާމަ ވަގުތުން ހުއްޓާ ލުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން އ.ދ. އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ކުރިއަށްދިޔަ ބަހުސްގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފަރާތުން ޝާޒޭ ދެ ފެއާ އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޑޮކްޓަރ އަލީ ނަސީރު މުހައްމަދު ދެއްކެވި ވާހަކަ ފުޅު ގައެވެ.

އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނާ ދެކޮޅަށް މިހާރު ކުރަމުންދާ ހަނގުރާމަ ވަގުތުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށް ގޮވައިލުމަށް ލާޒިމު ކޮށް ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ހުށަހެޅި ޤަރާރު 20 ފެބްރުއަރީ ގައި ވީޓޯ ކުރުމާ ގުޅިގެން އެ މައްސަލަ ބަހުސް ކުރުމަށް އ.ދ. ގެ އާންމު މަޖިލީހުގައި ބޭއްވި ބައްދަލު ވުމުގައި ވާހަކަ ފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން ޝާޒޭ ދެ ފެއާ އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޑޮކްޓަރ އަލީ ނަސީރު މުހައްމަދުގެ ވިދާޅުވީ އ.ދ. ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހުގައި ވީޓޯ ބޭނުންކުރުމުގެ ސަބަބުން އިސްރާއީލުން ހިންގާ އަމަލުތައް ކުރިއަށް ގެންދިއުމަށް ލިބުނު އިތުރު ހިތްވަރެއް ކަމަށެވެ. އަދި 29 ފެބްރުއަރީގައި ހިނގާ ދިޔަ ހާދިސާގައި އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ސަތޭކައަށް ވުރެ ގިނަ ރައްޔިތުން މަރާލައި، ޒަޚަމް ކޮށްފައިވާ ކަމަށާއި ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުން ފެނާއި ކާބޯތަކެތި އަދި އަސާސީ ބޭނުންތަކުން މަޙްރޫމް ކުރުމަށް ފަހު އިސްރާއީލުން އެ މީހުން މަރަމުން ގެންދިއުމަށް ހުއްޓުމެއް ނުގެނެވުމަކީ މުޅި ދުނިޔެ އެކަމާ ލަދު ގަންނަން ޖެހޭ ކަމެއް ކަމަށް ޝާޒޭ ދެ ފެއާ އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޑޮކްޓަރ އަލީ ނަސީރު މުހައްމަދު ގެ ވާހަކަ ފުޅުގައި އަލިއަޅުވާލެއްވިއެވެ.

ޝާޒޭ ދެ ފެއާ އެމްބެސެޑަރ ޑޮކްޓަރ އަލީ ނަސީރު މުހައްމަދު ގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނާ ދެކޮޅަށް ހިނގަމުންދާ ޖެނޮސައިޑް ހުއްޓުވުމަށް އަވަސް ފިޔަވަޅުތަކެއް އެޅުމަށް އ.ދ. ގެ ސަލާމަތީ މަޖިލީހަށް ގޮވާލެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި އިސްރާއީލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ދެމުންގެންދާ ހަމަލާތައް ވަގުތުން ހުއްޓުވައި ޖަވާބުދާރީކުރުމަށް ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މުޖުތަމައަށް ގޮވާލެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Maldives calls for urgent action to prevent Gaza genocide at the Extraordinary Meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
en.description: Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed delivered the national statement at the Extraordinary Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) held today in Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to discuss the Israeli aggression against the…
en.body:
Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr. Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed delivered the national statement at the Extraordinary Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) held today in Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to discuss the Israeli aggression against the Palestinian people.

During this meeting, the Maldives strongly condemned the violence in Gaza and the threats by the Israeli Government to attack Rafah. Reiterating the demand for an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the Maldives called on the international community to take decisive actions to prevent the acts of genocide in Gaza, which now amount to apartheid. The Maldives also urged for a stronger push to ensure an adequate volume of aid enters Gaza.

Reflecting on the oral submission delivered in support of Palestine on the Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem at the International Court of Justice, the Maldives also noted its intent to file a declaration of intervention in the case filed by South Africa. Reassuring its support for the Palestinian cause, the Maldives then stressed that the only means for lasting peace is the establishment of an independent and sovereign State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The Organization of Islamic Cooperation, comprising 57 Member States, has constantly advocated for the rights of the Palestinian people and a two-state solution to the decades long crisis. The Maldives has been an active member of the OIC since becoming a member in 1976.

dv.title: އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އޯ.އައި.ސީ.) ގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ކައުންސިލްގެ އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ޣައްޒާ 'ޖެނޮސައިޑް' ހުއްޓުވުމަށް އަވަސް ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އެޅުމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ގޮވާލައިފި
dv.description: އިސްރާއިލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާ ދެކޮޅަށް ދެމުންދާ ހަމަލާތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން، މިއަދު ސަޢުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ޖިއްދާގައި ބޭއްވި އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އޯ.އައި.ސީ.) ގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ކައުންސިލްގެ އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް އެފެއާޒް ޑޮކްޓަރު…
dv.body:
އިސްރާއިލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާ ދެކޮޅަށް ދެމުންދާ ހަމަލާތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން، މިއަދު ސަޢުދީ އަރަބިއްޔާގެ ޖިއްދާގައި ބޭއްވި އޯގަނައިޒޭޝަން އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް ކޯޕަރޭޝަން (އޯ.އައި.ސީ.) ގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުންގެ ކައުންސިލްގެ އެކްސްޓްރާއޯޑިނަރީ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އިސްލާމިކް އެފެއާޒް ޑޮކްޓަރު މުޙައްމަދު ޝަހީމް ޢަލީ ސަޢީދު ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފަރާތުން ޤައުމީ ބަޔާނެއް ދެއްވިއެވެ.

އިސްރާއިލުން ފަލަސްތީނުގައި ހިންގަމުންދާ 'ޖެނޮސައިޑް' ނުވަތަ ނަސްލު ނައްތާލުމުގެ ޢަމަލުތަކާއި އިސްރާއިލްގެ ސަރުކާރުން ރަފާއަށް ހަމަލާދޭނެކަމަށް ބުނަމުންދާ ބުނުން ހަރުކަށި އިބާރާތުން ކުށްވެރިކޮށް، މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އިން ވަނީ މިހާރުން މިހާރަށް ހަމަލާ ބަދަލުކުރުން ހުއްޓާލުމަށާއި އިސްރާއީލުން ހިންގަމުންދާ ލާއިންސާނީ ޢަމަލުތައް (އެޕާތައިޑް) ހުއްޓުވުމަށް ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މުޖުތަމަޢުން އަޅަންޖެހޭ ފިޔަވަޅުތައް އެޅުމަށް ގޮވާލާފައެވެ. އަދި، ޣައްޒާގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ބޭނުންވާ ކާބޯތަކެއްޗާއި އެހެނިހެން އަސާސީ ތަކެތި އެކަށީގެންވާ މިންވަރަށް ފޯރުކޮށްދިނުމަށް މިހާރަށްވުރެ ހަރުދަނާ ފިޔަވަޅުތަކެއް އެޅުމަށްވެސް ގޮވާލާފައިވެއެވެ.

މީގެއިތުރުން، އިރުމަތީ ޤުދުސް ހިމެނޭ ގޮތަށް، އިސްރާއީލުގެ ބާރުގެ ދަށަށް ގެނެސްފައިވާ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ބިންތަކުގައި ޢަމަލުކުރަމުންދާ އިސްރާއީލުގެ ސިޔާސަތުތަކާއި ހަމަތަކުން އުފެދޭ ޤާނޫނީ ނަތީޖާތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް ކޯޓް އޮފް ޖަސްޓިސް (އައި.ސީ.ޖޭ.) ގެ އިސްތިޝާރީ ލަފަޔަކަށް އެދި އ.ދ. ގެ ޢާންމު މަޖިލީހުން ހުށަހަޅާފައިވާ މައްސަލައިގައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހައްޤުގައި ހުށަހެޅި ބަޔާނަށް އަލިއަޅުވާލާފައިވެއެވެ. އަދި، ދެކުނު އެފްރިކާ އިން ހުށަހަޅާފައިވާ އެޕްލިކޭޝަންއަށް ޑިކްލަރޭޝަންއެއް ހުށަހަޅާނެކަމަށްވެސް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އިން ވަނީ ބަޔާންކޮށްފައެވެ. ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނާއެކު ދިވެހިން ދެމިތިބޭނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން ދީ، މި މައްސަލައަށް ދާއިމީ ހައްލެއް ލިބެން އޮތީ ފަލަސްތީނަކީ 1967 އަހަރުގެ ކުރިން އޮތް ސަރަޙައްދީ އިންތަކުގެ މައްޗަށް، އިރުމަތީ ގުދުސްއަކީ އެ ޤައުމުގެ ވެރިރަށް ކަމުގައި ކަނޑައަޅައިގެން، އުފެދިފައިވާ މުސްތަޤިއްލު މިނިވަން ދައުލަތެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ބަލައިގަނެގެންކަމަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ފާހަގަކުރިއެވެ.

އޯ.އައި.ސީ.އަކީ ފަލަސްތީނުގެ ހައްޤުގައި ވަކާލާތުކުރަމުން އަންނަ 57 މެމްބަރުން ހިމެނޭ ޖަމުޢިއްޔާއެކެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އޯ.އައި.ސީ.ގެ މެމްބަރަކަށްވެފައިވަނީ 1976 އެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer sends greetings to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria on the occasion of the Bulgarian Liberation Day
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Her Excellency Mariya Gabriel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria on the occasion of the Bulgarian Liberation Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Her Excellency Mariya Gabriel, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Bulgaria on the occasion of the Bulgarian Liberation Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Maldives, I am delighted to extend warm wishes to Your Excellency, the People and the Government of Bulgaria, on the joyous occasion of the Bulgarian Liberation Day.

I am certain that the friendly relations between our two countries will continue to enhance in the years to come.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration".

ENDS

en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Elmedin Konaković, on the occasion of the Independence Day of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

en.title: Maldives affirms its strong commitment to the promotion and protection of human rights at the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council
en.description: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sheryna Abdul Samad, today delivered the country statement at the High-level Segment of the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council. .
en.body:
The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sheryna Abdul Samad, today delivered the country statement at the High-level Segment of the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council. .

In her remarks, State Minister Sheryna highlighted the initiatives undertaken by the administration of President Dr. Mohamed Muizzu to support the promotion and protection of human rights. She further emphasised the importance given by the current administration to social issues such as gender equality, adequate housing, and disability inclusion.

In her statement, State Minister Sheryna also called for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and for the establishment of an independent and sovereign Palestinian State, based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

On behalf of the Government of Maldives, State Minister Sheryna reiterated the standing invitation to all special procedures mandate holders to visit the Maldives and reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to meet all its international human rights obligations and ensuring the realisation of human rights for all people.

The 55th Session of the Human Rights Council Session is being held from 26 February to 5 April 2024 in Geneva, Switzerland. The Maldives is a member of the Human Rights Council for the 2023 – 2025 term and actively engages in the Council.

ENDS
